reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Bitconnect as an opportunity to earn unusually high recurring returns, including claims of 10 to 30% monthly and daily returns of up to 2%, while demonstrating how to join and invest. The speaker presents personal earnings and directs viewers to a Bitconnect referral link, encouraging participation rather than warning, investigating, or merely reporting on the offer.

citations.quote: At the end of each day you can see my earning Daily one percent one and half percent Two percent I earn

opening.argument: The video contains a material qualification that undercuts treating it as an unequivocal promise of profit: the speaker reports that part of the process was “not working” and describes a specific Bitcoin transfer problem. That is consistent with a personal account of an imperfect process, not a guarantee that viewers will receive returns. The earnings language is also presented as the speaker’s own experience, while the supplied material does not establish that the figures were promised to every participant. A careful viewer could therefore understand this as a conditional, experience-based account with an evident warning that the process may fail.

The first time i invested this money was to $110 . After that i kept investing for $20

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited monthly and daily figures show what the speaker says happened, but they do not by themselves establish a guarantee or concealment of risk. The referral URL establishes a way to access the site, not that viewers were promised the same outcome. The referenced frame shows an account interface, but an interface is not proof that the offer was deceptive. The omitted qualification is that the speaker also explicitly reports the process was not working.

citations.quote: Daily one percent one and half percent Two percent I earn

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The failure comment is a troubleshooting observation, not a risk warning about losing money or a disclaimer that the advertised returns are unreliable. The speaker still says “you can earn 10 to 30 % monthly,” reports daily earnings, and describes continuing investment. Those statements frame the returns as an attractive earning opportunity; a technical problem does not neutralize the solicitation or make the claims conditional.

citations.quote: After that i kept investing for $20

opening.argument: The content can reasonably be understood as an operational demonstration of how the Bitconnect website works. The speaker says, “now let me show you,” then discusses account details, deposits and withdrawals, while the sampled frames show a phone displaying login, user-account, wallet, exchange and transaction screens. Showing a workflow and reporting one’s own experience is not the same as certifying that every advertised result is true. The supplied evidence supports a tutorial-style walkthrough of a cryptocurrency service, with viewers shown where the relevant functions appear and how the speaker used them.

citations.quote: now let me show you my e-mail id
If need to use bitcoin here. You can draw with Bitcoin deposis and Withdraw

rebuttal.rebuttal: The account screens do not prove the video's primary purpose was education rather than promotion. The speaker expressly connects the workflow to earning money, and the description supplies a referral URL. Still, those facts show how the service was presented, not that the speaker made a knowingly false statement or guaranteed a viewer's result. A demonstration can include personal earnings and access instructions without becoming proof of fraud.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not neutral merely because it uses screens. It explains how to join, fund and use the service while emphasizing recurring earnings, and it directs viewers toward participation through the supplied referral link. The screens show account and wallet functions, but they do not establish that the claimed earnings were genuine or sustainable. The operational detail therefore makes the solicitation actionable rather than merely educational.

citations.quote: If you have not money in the money account, then use bitcoin

opening.argument: At most, the evidence shows promotion of access to a cryptocurrency website and a referral-based service. The description contains a referral URL, and the frames show ordinary account, wallet and transaction interfaces. But the supplied material does not show a downline-income structure, a guaranteed repayment promise, or a request for credentials from viewers. The speaker discusses deposits, withdrawals and personal transactions, yet those operational features alone do not establish a scam mechanism. It is therefore reasonable to classify the presentation as ordinary service or referral promotion without certifying that the external service is safe.

citations.quote: If need to use bitcoin here. You can draw with Bitcoin deposis and Withdraw

rebuttal.rebuttal: The return claims make this more than a generic referral, but they do not establish the particular mechanisms asserted by a scam finding. The evidence does not show a downline scheme, guaranteed repayment language, or viewer credential harvesting. The frames display service functions and transaction history, while the referral link can be ordinary promotional routing. High stated returns may be questionable, but questionable is not the same as proof of deceptive operation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether every scam mechanism is visible. The video ties participation in the service to unusually high recurring returns, including monthly and daily figures, and supplies a referral path into that service. Deposits, withdrawals and account screens make the investment workflow actionable; they do not validate the returns. The absence of a visible downline or explicit guarantee does not negate the central earnings solicitation.
